title: Minimum Cost to Split into Ones II
summary: Given an integer n, find the minimum total cost to split it into n ones using operations that split an integer x into two positive integers a and b with a cost of a * b for each split.
statement: Given an integer n, find the minimum total cost to split it into n ones using operations that split an integer x into two positive integers a and b with a cost of a * b for each split.
constraints: Split a value x into positive a and b with a+b=x.
That split costs a*b; continue until all pieces are ones.
hints: A split adds a*b cross-pairs between its two groups.
Across the full split tree, each pair of final ones is separated exactly once.
Count unordered pairs among n ones.
The invariant is n choose two regardless of split order, so it is also the minimum.
editorial: The invariant is n choose two regardless of split order, so it is also the minimum.

tests.explanation: Splitting 3 into 1+2 costs two, then 2 into 1+1 costs one, totaling three.
Every complete sequence of splits costs six.
